subject: KiteWave evaluation — acceptance gates & ops alignment
messages_1_subject: KiteWave evaluation — acceptance gates & ops alignment
messages_1_body:
Thanks again for the call this morning — nice to meet the KiteWave team. Below is a concise recap and a proposed set of acceptance gates for the POC so we have a single source of truth ahead of kickoff.

High-level objective:
- Verify Redwood can be integrated into KiteWave's summarization pipeline with predictable latency, throughput, and unit economics while meeting quality thresholds for customer-facing output.

Suggested POC shape:
- Week 0 (2 business days): integration smoke (connect ingest, confirm logs, auth + routing)
- Weeks 1–2: functional evaluation (representative traffic, automated checks vs. golden prompts)
- Weeks 3–4: cost & ops validation (sustained throughput ramps, autoscaling, error handling)

Acceptance gates (measured during evaluation window):
- Latency: 95th-percentile end-to-end response time < 250ms for median prompt length (~256 tokens). Cold-starts will be tracked separately and summarized.
- Throughput: sustain 200 req/min with 95% of responses under the latency SLO on the baseline model variant.
- Cost: target effective cost per 1K output tokens ≤ $2.00 (approx. ≤ $0.002/token), measured with token-level accounting across the evaluation period.
- Quality: automated metrics + human review. Target: ≥85% acceptance rate on the review set across three canonical prompt families (abstractive summary, entity extraction, instruction-following). We'll source a 200-sample golden set from KiteWave.

Initial owners:
- Redwood runtime/integration: Karthik Iyer (tech lead)
- Redwood POC coordination & measurement: Monica Patel (CS)
- KiteWave technical owner: Alyssa Moreno (supply workload and traffic profile)

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Alyssa — please upload a representative sample workload (CSV) and the three canonical prompts by EOD 2027-06-21 so we can pre-seed quality checks.
2) Redwood — we'll send a draft SOW and the cost-estimate workbook by 2027-06-19 (attached).
3) Kickoff: propose Friday, 2027-06-24 for a 60-minute technical kickoff (integration, networking, security). Please flag if you need an earlier slot.

Attachments: kitewave_sample_workload.csv, kw_cost_estimate.xlsx, kitewave_poc_scope.pdf (attached).

If this matches your expectations, please reply with a quick confirmation and we'll lock the kickoff on the calendar.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

--

messages_2_subject: Re: KiteWave evaluation — acceptance gates & ops alignment
messages_2_body:
Thanks Dylan — this is helpful and aligns with our expectations. Quick notes from our side: 

- We'll upload a representative CSV by EOD Monday (contains ~1,500 historical requests, with token counts and response-type labels). Attached the initial sample extract.
- On the cost target: our internal bar was closer to $2.50/1K output tokens given current margins. We can test to your $2.00 target but would like Redwood to show the cost breakdown (compute vs networking vs model-level).
- Quality: we can deliver the 200-sample golden set; note that roughly 20% of our live prompts are longer (400–600 tokens). Can you confirm how that affects the latency SLO measurement?

Also, Tom (cc'd) will be our technical lead for network/VPC details. Tom — can you share the networking contact who'll coordinate firewall/VPN access?

Confirming the proposed kickoff on 2027-06-24 works for us, but suggest 14:00 PT to align with engineering.

Regards,
Alyssa Moreno
Head of Product — KiteWave

--

messages_3_subject: Re: KiteWave evaluation — acceptance gates & ops alignment
messages_3_body:
Appreciate the fast turnaround, Alyssa — and thanks for the sample extract. A few clarifications: 

- We will break down the cost estimate into model compute, infra overhead, and networking egress; the attached workbook shows our assumptions and a sensitivity table.
- For latency SLOs, we'll report both median/95p across your distribution and a separate bucket for long prompts (>400 tokens). For the official acceptance gate we'll call the 95p on the median-length bucket (<300 tokens) but include long-prompt performance in the final readout.
- 14:00 PT on 2027-06-24 is good for the kickoff; I'll send a calendar invite (link in related_links). Please include any network engineers who will own firewall rules.

Actioning: Karthik will prepare the runtime config suggestions and a list of model variants to test; Monica will draft the evaluation rubric and consent form for human review.

Thanks,
Dylan

Thanks,
Tom Hsu
